title: Implementation & Refactoring
description: Study make cohesive changes, preserve public contracts, handle errors explicitly, and review generated code critically. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Make cohesive changes
lessons.description: Identify all enforcement points needed for consistent behavior.
lessons.conceptOverview: A cohesive change addresses one behavioral goal across the necessary files. Avoid unrelated cleanup that obscures review, while still fixing all required paths for the requested behavior.
lessons.whyItMatters: Scope should include every required path for the intended change.

lessons.title: Preserve public contracts
lessons.description: Plan a compatibility mapping and migration test.
lessons.conceptOverview: Refactoring should preserve observable contracts unless a behavior change is intentional. Check call sites, serialization and persisted state before renaming or restructuring shared types.
lessons.whyItMatters: Public and persisted contracts extend beyond compile-time callers.

lessons.title: Handle errors explicitly
lessons.description: Design separate empty, denied and failed states.
lessons.conceptOverview: Distinguish validation errors, unavailable dependencies and unexpected failures. Preserve useful context without leaking sensitive values, and avoid converting failures into misleading success states.
lessons.whyItMatters: Failure states should not masquerade as valid empty results.

commonMistakes: Returning empty data is always an appropriate error fallback.

lessons.title: Review generated code critically
lessons.description: Verify the local API and replace the unsupported call.
lessons.conceptOverview: Treat suggested code as a candidate requiring inspection. Check assumptions, API compatibility and side effects; plausible syntax can hide incorrect semantics or invented dependencies.
lessons.whyItMatters: Generated code needs the same review as other code.
